messages:
maria: FYI we've got an urgent p95/p99 regression reported by a customer (ACME) — p95 up ~600ms -> 1.4s and p99 up to ~3.1s since ~11:03 UTC. Errors low, just huge queueing delays.
chantal: Which region/cluster?
maria: us-west-2, dedicated pool 3, tenant acme-prod. Support repro steps attached from customer: simple streaming chat sequence hitting /v1/chat with 4 tokens instantaneous but tail stalls.
alec: Looking at metrics — worker queue depth jumped ~x6 at 11:02, CPU on workers steady, but GPU utilization spiky on a small subset of pods. Might be a hot shard causing starvation.
jun: Logs show repeated admission rejections? I see admission_controller.throttle_count incrementing but not full failures. Means requests are being enqueued and piling behind concurrency gating.
oncall-bot: deploy 11:00 -> routing tweak rolled in; sharding config alpha-3 applied to pool-3 at 10:59 UTC (note: could be related).
maria: Customer provided a short curl to reproduce: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/chat 
 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
 -d '{"model":"gpt-4-mini","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"short"}],"stream":true}'
```
They say repeated quick calls create the tail latency.
alec: Repro locally by firing 200 concurrent short streaming requests against pool-3 — I see workers accumulating KV cache pressure and new requests waiting on admission slots.
achantal: Any quick mitigations we can ask customer to try? E.g., reduce concurrency, add jitter, or switch to non-streaming?
jun: Short-term mitigations: 1) increase per-pool concurrency limit (admission-config) by 20% for pool-3, 2) enable burstpad for that tenant so some requests can spill to burst capacity, or 3) route a small % to a compatible variant model with lower memory (gpt-4-mini-quant).
alec: I can flip admission-config to raise concurrency cap for pool-3, but want to avoid cascading OOMs. Will also add a temporary affinity rule to spread hot shard across more nodes.
maria: Please do the config change and ping when done, I'll relay to ACME and ask them to test. Also ask them to include request ids for slow calls.
oncall-bot: admission-config change queued: increase concurrency_limit pool-id=pool-3 from 120 -> 150 (manual override) by alec. Rollout starting...
alec: Done. Also rolled a soft-affinity change to re-balance queue owners, not a full deploy (no restart). Watching metrics.
jun: Watching logs — throttle_count dropped and queue depth halved within 30s. p95 back to ~250ms, p99 trending down to ~700ms.
maria: Customer confirmed substantial improvement after our change, but still sees occasional spikes when they burst. Suggested follow-ups: add automatic shard rebalancer, and add a circuit fallback to route to dedicated backup model when queue depth > threshold.
achantal: I'll open a ticket for product to discuss auto-rebalance and fallback. For now we should keep the manual override and schedule a controlled canary of the rebalancer.
alec: Filed ENG-REBAL-142: implement per-pool auto-reshard heuristic + emergency fallback routing. Putting a short postmortem note in incidents.
maria: Thanks — closing the loop with ACME and will monitor for 24h. :thumbsup:
